strings.d1.s0.name: Tegallalang Rice Terrace
strings.d1.s0.tips: Terraced rice fields, quiet and cool at 07:30. The swing is an optional 150,000 IDR.
strings.d1.s1.name: Tirta Empul
strings.d1.s1.tips: Holy spring purification temple. A sarong is provided, and the pool has 13 spouts.
strings.d1.s2.name: Ubud Palace
strings.d1.s2.tips: Royal palace courtyard with an evening legong dance (100,000 IDR).
strings.d1.s3.name: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka
strings.d1.s3.tips: Bourdain's roast pork, opposite the palace. It sells out by lunchtime.
strings.d1.s4.name: Ubud Monkey Forest
strings.d1.s4.tips: Sacred monkey forest and temples. Watch your glasses and bag.
strings.d1.b0.name: Warung Babi Guling Gung Cung
strings.d1.b0.tips: Local babi guling (roast suckling pig) near the palace.
strings.d1.b1.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk
strings.d1.b1.tips: A 2 km ridge walk, also good for sunset.
strings.d2.s0.name: Mount Batur Sunrise Trek
strings.d2.s0.tips: Can be slippery in the rainy season, and cloud is likely. A jeep tour is the alternative.
strings.d2.s1.name: Toya Devasya Hot Springs
strings.d2.s1.tips: Hot springs on the shore of Lake Batur, ideal after the trek.
strings.d2.s2.name: Ubud Art Market
strings.d2.s2.tips: Souvenir market. Start bargaining at half the asking price.
strings.d2.s3.name: Warung Biah Biah Ubud
strings.d2.s3.tips: Balinese tapas (small plates), local and good value.
strings.d2.s4.name: Saraswati Temple
strings.d2.s4.tips: Temple with a lotus pond, next to Starbucks.
strings.d2.b0.name: Warung Pulau Kelapa Ubud
strings.d2.b0.tips: Indonesian cuisine in a garden setting.
strings.d2.b1.name: Tegenungan Waterfall
strings.d2.b1.tips: Waterfall near Ubud, an alternative to the hot springs.
strings.d3.s0.name: Jatiluwih Rice Terraces
strings.d3.s0.tips: UNESCO-listed terraces, wider and calmer than Tegallalang, with walking routes.
strings.d3.s1.name: Ulun Danu Beratan Temple
strings.d3.s1.tips: The 'floating' temple on the lake, set against misty mountains.
strings.d3.s2.name: Jatiluwih Warung Dhea
strings.d3.s2.tips: Nasi campur (mixed rice plate) with terrace views.
strings.d3.s3.name: Tanah Lot
strings.d3.s3.tips: Rock temple in the sea. Sunset is the most famous time, and it gets crowded.
strings.d3.s4.name: Canggu Batu Bolong Beach
strings.d3.s4.tips: Canggu's beach bars: a beer after sunset and the lights of the surfers.
strings.d3.b0.name: Old Man's Canggu
strings.d3.b1.name: Handara Gate
strings.d3.b1.tips: The Instagram gate, next to the lake temple.
strings.d4.s0.name: Echo Beach Canggu
strings.d4.s0.tips: In the rainy season, morning is your window. Rubbish can wash in with the waves.
strings.d4.s1.name: Crate Cafe Canggu
strings.d4.s1.tips: Canggu's brunch culture, with smoothie bowls.
strings.d4.s2.name: Seminyak Village
strings.d4.s2.tips: Boutiques and a mall on Oberoi Street.
strings.d4.s3.name: Babi Guling Pak Malen Seminyak
strings.d4.s3.tips: Seminyak's babi guling (roast suckling pig), with crackling skin.
strings.d4.s4.name: Seminyak Beach Sunset
strings.d4.s4.tips: Ku De Ta or Potato Head beach club (minimum spend), or a beanbag on the sand for sunset.
strings.d4.b0.name: Potato Head Beach Club
strings.d4.b0.tips: Beach club with a pool and DJ.
strings.d4.b1.name: Petitenget Temple
strings.d4.b1.tips: Seminyak's temple, best on ceremony days.
strings.d5.s0.name: Kelingking Beach
strings.d5.s0.tips: Speedboat from Sanur takes 45 minutes, plus a vehicle tour (~900,000 IDR). T-rex rock and views from above (the descent takes 1 hour and is hard).
strings.d5.s1.name: Angel's Billabong
strings.d5.s1.tips: Natural pool. Swimming is forbidden at high tide.
strings.d5.s2.name: Broken Beach
strings.d5.s2.tips: Cove with a natural rock arch.
strings.d5.s3.name: Nusa Penida Warung Crystal Bay
strings.d5.s3.tips: Warung at Crystal Bay, serving nasi goreng (fried rice).
strings.d5.s4.name: Crystal Bay Snorkelling
strings.d5.s4.tips: See manta rays at Manta Point (boat ~200,000 IDR) or snorkel at Crystal Bay. Boat back at 16:00.
strings.d5.b0.name: Diamond Beach
strings.d5.b0.tips: White sand in east Penida, instead of snorkelling.
strings.d5.b1.name: Penida Colada Beach Bar
strings.d6.s0.name: Padang Padang Beach
strings.d6.s0.tips: Small cove reached through the rocks. Quiet in the morning, with monkeys.
strings.d6.s1.name: Bingin Beach Warung
strings.d6.s1.tips: Grilled fish at the cliffside warungs, reached by steps.
strings.d6.s2.name: Single Fin Uluwatu
strings.d6.s2.tips: Cliff bar for watching the surf and for lunch.
strings.d6.s3.name: Uluwatu Temple
strings.d6.s3.tips: Sea temple on a cliff. Monkeys snatch glasses, and a sarong is included.
strings.d6.s4.name: Kecak Fire Dance Uluwatu
strings.d6.s4.tips: Kecak performed by 100 people at sunset. Buy your ticket at 17:00 and sit at the front.
strings.d6.b0.name: Suluban Beach
strings.d6.b0.tips: Surf beach reached through a cave, instead of Padang Padang.
strings.d6.b1.name: Jimbaran Bay Seafood Grill
strings.d6.b1.tips: Seafood grilled on the sand, on the way back from Uluwatu.
strings.d7.s0.name: Sanur Beach Promenade
strings.d7.s0.tips: A 5 km seafront path. Sunrise is on Bali's east coast, with calm water.
strings.d7.s1.name: Sindhu Market Sanur
strings.d7.s1.tips: Morning market for bubur (rice porridge) and coffee.
strings.d7.s2.name: Sanur Village Spa
strings.d7.s3.name: Warung Mak Beng Sanur
strings.d7.s3.tips: Fried fish and soup since 1941, with a single set menu.
strings.d7.s4.name: Ngurah Rai Airport Transfer
strings.d7.s4.tips: The airport is 30 minutes away. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Genius Cafe Sanur
strings.d7.b1.name: Le Mayeur Museum Sanur
strings.d7.b1.tips: The Belgian painter's house, instead of the spa.
strings.note0: There is no public transport in Bali: use a scooter (international licence and helmet), Grab/Gojek or a car with a driver by the day (~700,000 IDR). Allow 1-2 hours of traffic between Ubud, Canggu and Uluwatu.
strings.note1: November to March is the rainy season: expect afternoon downpours, possible Penida boat cancellations and a cloudy Batur. Sightsee in the morning and save spas and cafes for later.
strings.note2: Temples require a sarong and sash (provided at the entrance). Women cannot enter during menstruation, and ceremony days call for respect.
strings.note3: Babi guling costs 40-60,000 IDR at a warung and nasi campur 30-50,000. Beach club minimum spend is 300-500,000.
strings.note4: Monkeys (Uluwatu, Monkey Forest) snatch glasses and phones. Don't show them food.
strings.note5: Take the Nusa Penida tour on the morning boat from Sanur. The Kelingking descent is hard, so the view from the top is enough.
